candidate.answerReason: Normalization gives \(p=1/200\). Seven squares have probability \(p\) each and three have probability \(3p\) each, giving \(16/200=0.08\).

methods.label: Normalize and add the square probabilities
methods.explanation:
First find \(p\) by adding the probabilities of all possible choices. There are 50 integers from 1 through 50 and 50 from 51 through 100, so
\[
50p+50(3p)=1,
\qquad p=\frac1{200}.
\]
The positive perfect squares at most 100 are exactly \(1^2,2^2,\ldots,10^2\), since \(10^2=100<11^2\). These are ten different integers. Because
\[
7^2=49\le50<64=8^2,
\]
seven of them have probability \(p\) each, and the remaining three have probability \(3p\) each.

Choosing one square excludes choosing any other square, so these probabilities add:
\[
P(\text{perfect square})
=7p+3(3p)
=\frac{16}{200}
=0.08.
\]
The answer is choice \(\mathrm{C}\).
